kept.spine: On market day the squares open to whoever brings something worth selling. The custom comes in by road, and the stalls are set out for what the road brings.
Soldiers of the town are kept here and the watch draws a wage. The garrison is a trade a man follows rather than a turn that comes round to a household.
The arguments in the taverns here run on who takes the higher seat rather than on the price of bread.
The trades here take on apprentices and the roofs are mended before they leak.
The walls are kept, the gates hang true, and nothing on either was built for the eye.
The town can man the wall and the towers together, and the ones who go up have gone up before.
Children here learn the rules about the dark before they learn their letters, and the rules have held.
The watch answers what is reported to it and does not go looking for the rest.
A price named here in the morning is the price named at dusk, whoever is doing the asking.
Somebody in the alchemists' quarter can do the work usually wanted, and the work past that is refused at the door.
The grain stores here are opened for trade and never for want.
The place stands on the way to somewhere else, and a plain living is made out of being where the carts stop.
What the town cannot grow comes up the road. A road that stops bringing it leaves the town on its own stores.
Rundgate is large enough that a man raised in one quarter walks into the next as a stranger.
The ties this town keeps with its neighbours run on trade and on nearness, and not one of them was forced on it by a grievance.
